verdictStatement: Zero blockers survive my own measurement. All three v1 blockers and all seven v1 advisories are repaired at their claimed pointers, at the v1 verdict's full width, and every repair was re-verified against primary bytes rather than the repairLog's word: I re-resolved the applied TypeScript authority myself (delivery.v4's 21 derivation operations over delivery.v2, none targeting either semantic substrate, so both substrates resolve to delivery.v2's bytes verbatim) and the repaired typescriptMajor1 cell matches those RESOLVED bytes character-for-character on all four quoted surfaces; the restated exhaustiveness invariant holds mechanically on the subject's own bytes; CC-1's seven-event universe now reaches both J-2 provider-fault constituents including the same-observation-instant tie under the class's exact-byte pass property. The diff account is exact - 16 changed leaves (the 14 repairedAt leaves plus artifact/version), 47 added, 0 removed, member order preserved, no silent edit and no phantom repairLog entry - and the repair-injected-defect hunt found none: crossCuttingEnforcement coheres with every refusal flow, the seven-event universe breaks no other class's closed-set claim, and the RF-8 assignment sits inside that family's original replay/downgrade scope. Two new advisories are recorded; neither blocks. With the repairs in, the artifact states at design level what the DR-102 acceptance cell names: measured provider bindings that are actually the TypeScript substrate's own bytes, a structural non-translation obligation proven byte-for-byte by the conformance classes rather than assumed from plumbing, and a hostile surface that can exercise every named join constituent.

findingSetDelta.B-CPC1-01: REPAIRED-VERIFIED. Re-resolved the applied authority myself: delivery.v4 (3cffece0...) derivedFrom names artifact delivery.v2.json at sha256 47b6cfd1... Against those resolved bytes, character-by-character: the transport quote equals $.typescriptSemanticSubstrate.providerProtocol.transport exactly; the stdout quote equals .providerProtocol.stdout exactly; closedHostToWorkerFrames[0]='Hello' and [6]='Cancel' as the cell states; providerProtocol.major=1; and the fourteen-field list equals $.typescriptSemanticSubstrate.identity.handshakeRequired name-for-name in order. No Rust residue remains under the TS heading: the Rust transport string ('length-delimited canonical CBOR over inherited stdin/stdout'), rustCommitHash, and sysrootDigest are all absent from the cell. The untouched rustMajor2 cell was spot-checked against the Rust artifacts rather than trusted from v1: in rust-provider-protocol.v4.json (3e349347..., re-measured) Hello and HelloAck are frame-type enum members [0] and [1], stdout-byte is event-kind enum member [6], and stdout-byte appears in transition rules 26/27 and in fallbackRule.mustCoverEventKinds - the cell's claim is true in the restated context.

CC-1's universe is now the seven-event set {cancel-issued, provider-final-octet, control-fault, provider-fault-report, provider-EOF, process-death, teardown-initiated}; provider-fault-report is defined as the owning participant's fault report - J-2's second provider-fault constituent, the exact gap B-CPC1-03 named - injected as a boundary report whose content the control plane never reads; the intent requires every J-2 variant in which the provider fault is the fault report rather than an EOF, names the same-observation-instant tie J-2 resolves control-fault-first (matching J-2's own tie rule), and keeps the exact-byte pass property (injected stream equal byte-for-byte in every ordering). All eleven ridden or routed rows now carry recorded standings, and every one re-verified cell-for-cell against file 08 at f0d72536... The DR-G21 paraphrase 'PROPOSED and expressly short of release standing' was judged against the cell's actual words: 'PROPOSED; not QUALIFIED' - the paraphrase asserts nothing the cell does not (QUALIFIED is this corpus's release-qualification standing, and the negation is express in the cell), and by paraphrasing it also keeps the artifact's QUALIFIED-vocabulary discipline intact.
findingSetDelta.A-CPC1-05: REPAIRED-VERIFIED and coherent with RF-8's original scope. The mismatched-helloAck controlMajor is assigned to RF-8 at all three claimed pointers (families[7].covers, handshake step 2 body, CC-6 intent), the three cross-references agree, and the assignment sits inside the family's own name and prior coverage (handshake-replay-or-downgrade; in-channel version movement IS the downgrade/renegotiation attempt in wire form). The 'detected host-side' claim is true: helloAck flows component-to-host on fd4. The CC-6 fixture's typed outcome is now determined.
findingSetDelta.A-CPC1-06: REPAIRED-VERIFIED as genuine foreclosure, not a re-promise. octetIdentityProperty acknowledges POSIX-pipe write-boundary non-preservation, restates the enforceable frame obligation at the in-band framing layer, and forecloses carrier-write-boundary-sensitive subprotocols on this transport outright (admission requires an explicit transport-changing successor); CC-9 declares such a fixture a fixture-design error, not a conformance dimension. The premise that both existing majors frame in-band was verified at bytes: TS major 1 transport is 'length-delimited canonical CBOR on stdin/stdout' (delivery.v2 resolved), and the merged Rust base's framing member specifies uint64-big-endian payloadLength, then 32 raw SHA-256 digest bytes, then the canonical-CBOR payload (rust-provider-protocol.v2.json) - length-delimited, in-band, recoverable from the octet stream.
findingSetDelta.A-CPC1-07: REPAIRED-VERIFIED. The false bounds-discipline rationale is removed from framing.sequencing; the uint53/RF-7 rule stands as a bare enforced constant. The replacement caveat was itself hard-compared per freeze 7.2.2.1 (a caveat is a measurement): 'this contract binds no per-channel frame-count bound' is true - the only frame-count clause in the file is this sentence itself.

advisories.finding: The measured sentence 'the operation list holds 21 operations; none names any path under typescriptSemanticSubstrate or rustSemanticSubstrate' fails hard-comparison replication under its plainest reading: delivery.v4 operations [17] and [18] (add capabilityManifestIdentity / capabilityManifestCustody) carry VALUES whose prose and JSONPath lists literally name paths under typescriptSemanticSubstrate (e.g. '$.typescriptSemanticSubstrate.providerProtocol.wireSchema.commitments.domainRule' inside positionsUnderPredicateA), so a reviewer replicating the measurement by searching the operation list finds five such namings. The operative claim is true and load-bearing exactly as needed: no operation's TARGET path lies under either substrate, none of the 21 operations mentions the quoted leaves (providerProtocol.transport/stdout, closedHostToWorkerFrames, handshakeRequired), and the substrates therefore resolve to delivery.v2's bytes verbatim - the mentions are citations inside added members, mentioning not carrying. A successor should say 'targets' or 'applies to' rather than 'names' so the measurement replicates as stated (freeze 7.2.2 class, benign in direction).

advisories.clause: hostileDualChannelConformance CC-1 intent versus J-1's tie rule
advisories.finding: The repaired CC-1 names one same-observation-instant tie as exercised - J-2's, resolved control-fault-first - but J-1 also defines a same-observation-instant tie with the opposite polarity (the data-plane event is appended first: 'a byte that has arrived is history'), and no fixture obligation names injecting it. The repair itself demonstrates the authors' position that tie coverage must be NAMED to be part of the class's obligation ('every pairwise and every reachable total ordering' enumerates orderings, and the J-2 tie was added explicitly rather than read out of that clause); by that same standard the J-1 tie, and same-instant configurations of the other event pairs the seven-event universe makes reachable, are unnamed. Advisory, not blocker: J-1's tie rule is normatively defined in the join table, both J-2 provider-fault constituents are now reachable events, and a harness reading CC-1 in good faith can exercise the J-1 tie under the existing exact-byte pass property - but the hostile half's specification should name it the way it now names J-2's.

verifiedClean.registerCellJudgment: With the repairs in, the artifact states the DR-102 acceptance-evidence cell's content at design level: the measured provider transport bindings are now genuinely the TypeScript substrate's own resolved bytes and the verified Rust merge's enums; the non-translation obligation is structural (control plane never holds provider octets) and proven byte-for-byte by CC-1/CC-2/CC-9 rather than assumed; the capability envelope is closed and its exhaustiveness invariant is mechanically true; every constituent of the five named joins - including both J-2 provider-fault forms - is a reachable event of the hostile surface. What remains open is what the artifact itself routes: execution of the classes is DR-G21/ID-DEP-3 territory and the cell discharges only when a harness runs them, which this candidate states rather than hides (whatThisDoesNotDo items 4 and 10). Nothing missing at design level was found beyond the two advisories above.
